core_obligations: Show (1) implies (2) immediately, and prove (2) implies (1) by induction on the length, with the two-element case handled by identifying two kernels (proof lines 17026-17042).
Prove (2) implies (3) by exhibiting, for each subset of the variables, that the next element is a nonzerodivisor on the corresponding quotient in the polynomial ring (proof lines 17042-17060).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the two-element case and run the induction (proof lines 17026-17042).
Transfer regularity to the polynomial ring (proof lines 17042-17061).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a sequence which does not generate the unit ideal, regularity of every permutation, of every subsequence and of the sequence multiplied by the variables in the polynomial ring are equivalent (statement lines 17013-17024). The proof does not use the Koszul complex: it reduces to the two-element case by identifying two kernels, runs an induction on the length for the permutation statement, and then transfers regularity to the polynomial ring by checking each element on the relevant quotient (proof lines 17026-17061). The kernel identification in the two-element case is the step that starts the induction. H2.
